intro: Hands-on AZ-104 labs graded in your browser: an Azure CLI (Cloud Shell) simulator for networking, storage, RBAC, peering, VMs, tags and locks, plus a monitoring console for alerts. Simulated, so some commands and outputs are simplified; nothing touches a real subscription.

labs.title: Build a VNet with subnets and an NSG
labs.summary: Use the Azure CLI to create a resource group, a VNet with two subnets, and an NSG that allows HTTPS to the web subnet.
labs.scenario:
In Cloud Shell, build the network for a new app:

  • Resource group rg-net-lab in eastus
  • VNet vnet-app with address space 10.20.0.0/16
  • Subnets snet-web 10.20.1.0/24 and snet-db 10.20.2.0/24
  • NSG nsg-web with an inbound rule Allow-HTTPS (priority 100) allowing TCP 443 from Internet
  • Associate nsg-web with snet-web

tasks.text: Resource group rg-net-lab in eastus
VNet vnet-app with 10.20.0.0/16
Subnets snet-web (10.20.1.0/24) and snet-db (10.20.2.0/24)
NSG nsg-web allows inbound TCP 443 from Internet at priority 100
nsg-web is associated with snet-web

hints: Every command starts with az. Add -o table to list commands for readable output.
az network vnet create -g rg-net-lab -n vnet-app --address-prefixes 10.20.0.0/16 --subnet-name snet-web --subnet-prefixes 10.20.1.0/24

az network nsg rule create -g rg-net-lab --nsg-name nsg-web -n Allow-HTTPS --priority 100 --direction Inbound --access Allow --protocol Tcp --destination-port-ranges 443 --source-address-prefixes Internet
az network vnet subnet update -g rg-net-lab --vnet-name vnet-app -n snet-web --network-security-group nsg-web
labs.solution:
az group create -n rg-net-lab -l eastus
az network vnet create -g rg-net-lab -n vnet-app --address-prefixes 10.20.0.0/16 --subnet-name snet-web --subnet-prefixes 10.20.1.0/24
az network vnet subnet create -g rg-net-lab --vnet-name vnet-app -n snet-db --address-prefixes 10.20.2.0/24
az network nsg create -g rg-net-lab -n nsg-web
az network nsg rule create -g rg-net-lab --nsg-name nsg-web -n Allow-HTTPS --priority 100 --direction Inbound --access Allow --protocol Tcp --destination-port-ranges 443 --source-address-prefixes Internet
az network vnet subnet update -g rg-net-lab --vnet-name vnet-app -n snet-web --network-security-group nsg-web
labs.review: Subnets must sit inside the VNet's address space without overlapping. NSG rules are evaluated by priority (lower first), and associating an NSG with a subnet applies it to every NIC in that subnet.

labs.title: Secure a storage account
labs.summary: Create a zone-redundant StorageV2 account with secure defaults, add a private container, and fix an insecure legacy account.
labs.scenario:
Resource group rg-data already exists and contains an older account, stlegacy01, that allows public blob access and TLS 1.0.

  • Create stfinance01: StorageV2, Standard_ZRS, HTTPS only, minimum TLS 1.2, no public blob access
  • Add a private container named invoices
  • Update stlegacy01: minimum TLS 1.2 and no public blob access

tasks.text: stfinance01 is StorageV2 with Standard_ZRS
stfinance01: HTTPS only, TLS 1.2 minimum, no public blob access
A private container invoices exists in stfinance01
stlegacy01 now requires TLS 1.2 and blocks public blob access
Which redundancy option protects against a single datacenter (zone) failure but keeps data in one region?

hints: Every command starts with az. Add -o table to list commands for readable output.
az storage account create -n stfinance01 -g rg-data --sku Standard_ZRS --kind StorageV2 --https-only true --min-tls-version TLS1_2 --allow-blob-public-access false
az storage container create --account-name stfinance01 -n invoices --public-access off --auth-mode login
labs.solution:
az storage account create -n stfinance01 -g rg-data -l eastus --sku Standard_ZRS --kind StorageV2 --https-only true --min-tls-version TLS1_2 --allow-blob-public-access false
az storage container create --account-name stfinance01 -n invoices --public-access off --auth-mode login
az storage account update -n stlegacy01 -g rg-data --min-tls-version TLS1_2 --allow-blob-public-access false
labs.review: LRS keeps three copies in one datacenter, ZRS spreads them across availability zones in a region, and GRS/GZRS add a secondary region. Disabling public blob access at the account level overrides container-level public settings.

labs.title: Apply least-privilege RBAC
labs.summary: Grant scoped built-in roles to a user and a group, and remove an over-privileged contractor assignment.
labs.scenario:
Access review findings for subscription Contoso-Lab (ID 6f1c2a9e-3b4d-4e5f-9a8b-7c6d5e4f3a21):

  • alex@contoso.com needs to view (not change) everything in rg-app
  • The Operations group (object ID 8d2c6b1e-4f3a-4e2b-9c1d-7a6b5c4d3e2f) manages VMs in rg-app but not their networks or storage
  • contractor@fabrikam.com has Owner on the whole subscription; the contract ended

tasks.text: Review current assignments with az role assignment list
alex has Reader on rg-app (not the subscription)
The Operations group has Virtual Machine Contributor on rg-app
The contractor no longer has any role
priya's Owner assignment is untouched

hints: Every command starts with az. Add -o table to list commands for readable output.
az role assignment create --assignee alex@contoso.com --role Reader -g rg-app scopes the role to the resource group.
Quote role names with spaces: --role "Virtual Machine Contributor".
az role assignment delete --assignee contractor@fabrikam.com --role Owner --scope /subscriptions/…
labs.solution:
az role assignment list -o table
az role assignment create --assignee alex@contoso.com --role Reader -g rg-app
az role assignment create --assignee 8d2c6b1e-4f3a-4e2b-9c1d-7a6b5c4d3e2f --role "Virtual Machine Contributor" -g rg-app
az role assignment delete --assignee contractor@fabrikam.com --role Owner --scope /subscriptions/6f1c2a9e-3b4d-4e5f-9a8b-7c6d5e4f3a21
labs.review: Assign the narrowest built-in role at the narrowest scope that works, prefer groups over individuals, and remove access promptly when it's no longer needed.

labs.title: Connect VNets with peering
labs.summary: Peer a hub and a spoke VNet in both directions and explain why an overlapping VNet can't be peered.
labs.scenario: Hub vnet-hub (10.0.0.0/16, rg rg-hub) hosts shared services. Peer it with spoke vnet-spoke1 (10.1.0.0/16, rg rg-spoke1). Traffic from the hub's firewall appliance must be accepted by the spoke. A third network, vnet-legacy (10.0.0.0/20), also wants to connect to the hub.

tasks.text: Peering from vnet-hub to vnet-spoke1
Peering from vnet-spoke1 to vnet-hub that allows forwarded traffic
Check that the peering shows Connected
Why can't vnet-legacy peer with vnet-hub?

questions.prompt: vnet-legacy can't peer with vnet-hub because:
options: Their address spaces overlap (10.0.0.0/20 is inside 10.0.0.0/16)

hints: Every command starts with az. Add -o table to list commands for readable output.
Peering is created separately on each side; it shows Connected only when both exist.

az network vnet peering create -g rg-spoke1 -n spoke1-to-hub --vnet-name vnet-spoke1 --remote-vnet vnet-hub --allow-vnet-access --allow-forwarded-traffic (outside this lab, use the hub's full resource ID for --remote-vnet when it's in another resource group).
labs.solution:
az network vnet peering create -g rg-hub -n hub-to-spoke1 --vnet-name vnet-hub --remote-vnet vnet-spoke1 --allow-vnet-access
az network vnet peering create -g rg-spoke1 -n spoke1-to-hub --vnet-name vnet-spoke1 --remote-vnet vnet-hub --allow-vnet-access --allow-forwarded-traffic
az network vnet peering list -g rg-hub --vnet-name vnet-hub -o table
labs.review: VNet peering needs a link on both sides and non-overlapping address spaces. Allow forwarded traffic lets a spoke accept traffic that a hub appliance forwards on behalf of other networks. Peering isn't transitive between spokes.

labs.title: Deploy and manage a private VM
labs.summary: Create an Ubuntu VM with no public IP in an existing subnet, attach a data disk, resize it, and stop billing for compute when idle.
labs.scenario:
Resource group rg-compute has VNet vnet-prod with subnet snet-app. Deploy vm-app01:

  • Image Ubuntu2204, size Standard_B2s, admin azureuser with SSH keys
  • In vnet-prod/snet-app with no public IP (it's reached through Bastion)
  • Attach a new 128 GB data disk named disk-app01-data
  • Load testing shows it needs more CPU: resize to Standard_D2s_v5
  • It's only used in business hours: deallocate it now so compute stops billing

tasks.text: vm-app01 runs Ubuntu2204 in vnet-prod/snet-app
It has no public IP address
A 128 GB data disk is attached
It's resized to Standard_D2s_v5
It's deallocated (not just stopped)

hints: Every command starts with az. Add -o table to list commands for readable output.
--public-ip-address "" creates the VM without a public IP.
az vm disk attach -g rg-compute --vm-name vm-app01 --name disk-app01-data --new --size-gb 128
A stopped VM still bills for compute; a deallocated VM doesn't.
labs.solution:
az vm create -g rg-compute -n vm-app01 --image Ubuntu2204 --size Standard_B2s --admin-username azureuser --generate-ssh-keys --vnet-name vnet-prod --subnet snet-app --public-ip-address ""
az vm disk attach -g rg-compute --vm-name vm-app01 --name disk-app01-data --new --size-gb 128
az vm resize -g rg-compute -n vm-app01 --size Standard_D2s_v5
az vm deallocate -g rg-compute -n vm-app01
labs.review: Keep management traffic private with Bastion instead of public IPs, size VMs from measured load, and deallocate idle VMs because stopped-but-allocated VMs still incur compute charges.

labs.title: Tag and lock production resources
labs.summary: Tag a resource group for cost reporting and protect it with a CanNotDelete lock, then confirm the lock works.
labs.scenario:
Finance needs cost reports by environment and cost center, and last month someone deleted a production resource group by mistake. For rg-prod:

  • Tags env=prod and costCenter=4410
  • A lock named lock-prod-nodelete that prevents deletion but still allows changes
  • Prove it: try to delete the resource group

tasks.text: rg-prod has tags env=prod and costCenter=4410
A CanNotDelete lock named lock-prod-nodelete is on rg-prod
A delete attempt on rg-prod is blocked
Choose the lock that would also block changes

questions.prompt: Which lock level blocks both deletes and modifications?

hints: Every command starts with az. Add -o table to list commands for readable output.
az group update -n rg-prod --tags env=prod costCenter=4410 replaces the tag set; --set tags.env=prod adds one tag.
az lock create -n lock-prod-nodelete --lock-type CanNotDelete -g rg-prod
labs.solution:
az group update -n rg-prod --set tags.env=prod tags.costCenter=4410
az lock create -n lock-prod-nodelete --lock-type CanNotDelete -g rg-prod
az group delete -n rg-prod --yes      # fails: the scope is locked
labs.review: Tags drive cost reporting and automation. CanNotDelete still allows changes; ReadOnly blocks writes too (and can break operations like listing storage keys). Locks apply to everyone, including Owners.

labs.title: Create a CPU alert with an action group
labs.summary: Configure a metric alert rule and an action group in a cloud monitoring console.
labs.scenario: The ops team wants an email when vm-app01 averages more than 80% CPU over 5 minutes, evaluated every minute, at severity 2 (warning). Notifications go to an action group ag-ops that emails ops@contoso.com. Save each page.

tasks.text: Action group ag-ops emails ops@contoso.com
The rule targets vm-app01 on Percentage CPU (Average)
Greater than 80 over 5 minutes, checked every minute
Severity 2, uses ag-ops, enabled, and has a name

hints: Save the action group page before selecting it on the rule page (both are graded on saved values).
labs.solution: Action group: ag-ops, ops@contoso.com. Alert rule: vm-app01, Percentage CPU, Average, Greater than, 80, 5 minutes, 1 minute, name e.g. cpu-high-vm-app01, 2 - Warning, ag-ops, enabled.
labs.review: Metric alerts combine a signal, aggregation, operator, threshold, window and frequency. Action groups hold the notifications and actions so many rules can reuse them.
